meta.title: Powered Silicon Weekly Dashboard
meta.baseline_note: Persistent weekly state updated through Oct. 2, 2026. The Sep. 25 weekly checkpoint is backfilled from source-verified developments because the prior persistent Library snapshot ended Sep. 18.
meta.thesis: Irreversible AI power and physical-infrastructure commitments imply future silicon demand; during a chip upcycle, the sell clock starts when hardware delivery accelerates faster than energizable IT capacity.

action_rules.0-2: ACCUMULATE / ADD on weakness while irreversible infrastructure continues

notes: Model windows are empirical working ranges, not disclosed contractual lead times.

A power project is counted as implied compute only after capital becomes materially irreversible: executed equipment purchase, funded EPC, firm utility/PPA/interconnection, or physical construction with a credible COD.
Announced or queued GW without hard commitments are excluded from the buy clock.
Sell score counts independent active categories, not repeated headlines about the same condition.

current_signals.headline: Amazon seeks external financing against ~$8B of deployed NVIDIA chips
current_signals.metric: Financial Times reports Amazon plans an SPV around roughly $8B of Grace Blackwell chips already deployed across more than a dozen data centers in five U.S. states, with leaseback economics.
current_signals.read: Capital recycling around already-deployed hardware reinforces scale and delivery intensity but is not a new chip order and does not add another sell point.

current_signals.headline: Enerflex wins ~450 MW behind-the-meter generation-equipment contract
current_signals.metric: Contracted to design, engineer, fabricate and assemble approximately 450 MW of natural-gas-fired generation units; deliveries begin in 2027 and finish in 2028.
current_signals.read: Hard BUY-clock addition with a bounded equipment-delivery window. Site/customer and data-hall COD are undisclosed; modeled usable IT is an estimate from generation capacity, not a disclosed IT load.

current_signals.headline: JERA, Dell and RHAELM sign MoU for up to 400 MW Chiba AI campus
current_signals.metric: Project targets operations around 2028, >$15B total capital deployment and up to 400 MW behind-the-meter capacity at JERA Chiba; Apollo intends to serve as financing partner.
current_signals.read: Important pipeline, but the announcement is an MoU and uses expected/intended financing language. It is excluded from the hard BUY clock and coverage denominator until binding financing/power/customer/EPC commitments are disclosed.

current_signals.headline: Nebius signs binding 12-year agreement for 50 MW critical IT at power-secured CLT1
current_signals.metric: 50 MW critical IT backed by 65 MW 15-year electric-service agreement; ESA service scheduled Oct. 1, 2026; hall 1 target ~month 10 (25 MW) and hall 2 ~month 14 (25 MW).
current_signals.read: Excellent dual-clock signal: hard customer + utility power, while the disclosed 10-14 month conversion from utility service to 50 MW critical IT demonstrates physical build-throughput lag.

current_signals.headline: Amazon signs 20-year 690 MW nuclear agreement supporting 190 MW uprate
current_signals.metric: Agreement supports >$3B of Maryland infrastructure investment; includes 690 MW of power and ~190 MW of new generation expected 2030-2032.
current_signals.read: Long-dated irreversible power. Only the 190 MW uprate is incremental generation; the full 690 MW is not treated as new usable IT capacity and power continues to flow through PJM.

current_signals.headline: Micron revenue accelerates sharply again into AI-driven fiscal 2027
current_signals.metric: FQ4 revenue $54.23B vs $41.46B in FQ3 and $11.32B a year earlier; management points to Strategic Customer Agreements and increased technology/manufacturing investment.
current_signals.read: Fresh, strong confirmation that chip-revenue acceleration remains active. It reinforces rather than adds to the existing chip-revenue sell point.

current_signals.headline: FERC acts on PJM reliability backstop tied to zones with data-center growth
current_signals.metric: FERC order/concurrence supports reliability backstop procurement and cost assignment to zones responsible for resource-adequacy shortfalls; state large-load tariffs/collateral remain part of the response.
current_signals.read: System intervention remains active; this is not a new point because the category was already on.

current_signals.headline: $1.17B take-or-pay AMD GPU infrastructure orders set dated deployments
current_signals.metric: Initial MI355X deployment has contractual start date Dec. 31, 2026; second MI455X deployment starts Jun. 30, 2027; ~$133M contractual prepayments.
current_signals.read: Direct dated GPU-demand commitment; reinforces chip acceleration. GPU counts/configuration are not disclosed, so no MW conversion.

current_signals.headline: CleanSpark closes $2.276B secured financing for Sandersville build-out
current_signals.metric: Senior secured notes closed; proceeds fund remaining data-center build-out. The underlying 20-year lease is for 175 MW of critical IT load with deliveries expected to begin Q4 2027.
current_signals.read: Hardens an existing lease into funded construction. The 175 MW critical IT load is disclosed by CleanSpark; financing close is economically irreversible.

current_signals.headline: Oracle issues force-majeure notice as Project Jupiter gas pipeline slips about six months
current_signals.metric: Pipeline intended to supply the 2.45 GW campus shifted to Feb. 1, 2027 after permit denials; Oracle says the 2028 campus schedule remains on plan.
current_signals.read: Activates power/COD/construction slippage. The campus is not canceled; this is schedule-risk evidence, not a claim that 2028 COD has already slipped.

current_signals.headline: Anthropic commits $11.6B over seven years; Akamai plans ~$5.5B related capex
current_signals.metric: Akamai adds ~$1.7B of 2026 capex to secure/pre-purchase critical components including memory; total deal-related capex ~ $5.5B.
current_signals.read: Hard compute demand and front-loaded component procurement. Reinforces server/hardware acceleration but does not add a separate sell point beyond the category.

current_signals.project: Powered Land / Powered Shell AI portfolio - 2G tranche
current_signals.headline: Energy Vault places a separate 275 MW 2G generation-system order
current_signals.metric: 275 MW containerized generation order; deliveries planned Q4 2027 through Q3 2028; long-term service included.
current_signals.read: Hard equipment purchase with dated delivery window. Treated as distinct from Energy Vault's Sep. 10 Rolls-Royce MTU 275 MW tranche because 2G describes it as another order.

current_signals.headline: Supermicro begins shipping production Vera Rubin NVL72 racks
current_signals.metric: Rubin NVL72 racks are shipping; Supermicro blueprint defines a 5 MW-to-GW deployment stack and a 1,152-GPU / 16-rack Scalable Unit.
current_signals.read: Confirms server/rack delivery acceleration remains active. Blueprint scale is not treated as shipped quantity, so no hardware-equivalent MW is manufactured.

current_signals.headline: 20-year PPA secures 200-207 MW for Phase 1
current_signals.metric: Executed PPA for a minimum 200 MW and maximum 207 MW from Vistra/Luminant for the Odessa-area Texas Critical Data Center.
current_signals.read: Hard BUY-clock commitment. Power is contractually secured; exact delivery/COD date is not public, so no time-bounded IT-MW denominator or silicon window is inferred.

current_signals.headline: Kodiak signs six-year 76 MW behind-the-meter baseload power agreement
current_signals.metric: 76 MW, ~40 reciprocating gas units; deployment begins Q4 2026 and scales into Q1 2027; data-center operator is contracted with an investment-grade hyperscaler and has a GPU designer guarantor.
current_signals.read: Near-term hard denominator. Using the standing 95% availability / 85% reserve / 1.15 PUE assumptions yields ~53 MW modeled usable IT capacity; this is an estimate, not a disclosed IT-load figure.

current_signals.headline: Crusoe closes initial $3.9B Series F; reports >6 GW gross contracted capacity and >1 GW operational
current_signals.metric: Initial $3.9B Series F closed at $30.9B post-money valuation; >$140B TCV; >6 GW gross contracted across data centers and cloud, including >1 GW delivered and operational.
current_signals.read: Funding close increases execution capacity, but the >6 GW aggregate mixes projects and lacks time-bounded site-level delivery schedules. It is tracked as funded capacity support, not added to the usable-power denominator.

current_signals.project: Amazon global data-center backup generation program
current_signals.headline: Amazon locks long-term Generac backup-generator supply; $2.4B of initial deliveries expected in 2027-28
current_signals.metric: Executed long-term supply agreement. Initial backup-generator deliveries expected to total $2.4B in 2027-2028; warrant vesting is linked to Amazon payments for data-center backup generators up to $8B.
current_signals.read: NEW HARD BUY-CLOCK COMMITMENT: executed power-equipment supply with dated delivery economics. Units, MW, sites and generator configurations are not disclosed, so it strengthens the physical denominator qualitatively but is excluded from MW coverage calculations.

current_signals.headline: CoreWeave converts Niagara Falls LOI into a definitive 15-year anchor lease plus expansion agreement
current_signals.metric: Definitive lease replaces the June 30 non-binding LOI; 15-year initial term with two five-year renewal options. Campus has an existing grid interconnection and is being adapted for high-density liquid-cooled AI infrastructure.
current_signals.read: Hardens a previously tentative capacity commitment. Exact leased IT MW, capacity-delivery dates and expansion power are not yet disclosed, so no MW denominator or silicon-conversion window is manufactured.

current_signals.headline: CoreWeave brings a multi-rack Vera Rubin NVL72 cluster into production
current_signals.metric: Hundreds of Rubin GPUs are connected as one scale-out production cluster; each NVL72 rack contains 72 Rubin GPUs. CoreWeave says only racks that clear system validation move into production.
current_signals.read: Reinforces the already-active server/rack delivery category. It does not add a fourth sell point because server delivery acceleration was already active. Exact rack count and electrical draw are not disclosed, so no MW conversion.

current_signals.headline: AI Energy Management Alliance launches around flexible, grid-responsive AI data centers
current_signals.metric: Alliance aims to let AI data centers dynamically manage power draw to unlock faster and larger grid connections while supporting reliability.
current_signals.read: This is a mitigation response to the grid-integration constraint, not evidence that the constraint has cleared. The system-intervention sell category remains active but receives no additional point.

current_signals.headline: Crusoe opens a second 400,000-square-foot Tulsa factory for AI electrical infrastructure
current_signals.metric: New facility makes medium-voltage switchgear, low-voltage switchboards, electrical enclosures, controls and busbar; Crusoe says Tulsa has supplied >2,500 switchboards to Stargate Abilene.
current_signals.read: Positive throughput signal rather than a warning: in-house electrical manufacturing capacity expanded. This does not activate the build-throughput-gap sell category.

current_signals.headline: PJM proposes new reliability standards after ~4 GW data-center load disconnection event
current_signals.metric: Nearly 4,000 MW of Northern Virginia data-center load unexpectedly disconnected July 22; PJM says it was the third measurable event in two years and plans new ride-through requirements.
current_signals.read: NEW SELL CATEGORY: system-level integration stress is now active. This moves the sell clock from 2/5 to 3/5; do not count ERCOT separately because both are the same category.

current_signals.headline: Oracle delivered 850 MW of additional data-center capacity and >300,000 GPUs in Q1
current_signals.metric: Q1 OCI IaaS revenue +121% YoY to $7.4B; >300,000 GPUs delivered since Q4, nearly 3x Q4 capacity; 850 MW additional data-center capacity delivered; RPO $664B.
current_signals.read: Strong confirmation that the current hardware wave is converting into deployed capacity and revenue. It reinforces server/rack acceleration but does not add a new sell category.

current_signals.company: Energy Vault / Eagle Point / Rolls-Royce MTU
current_signals.headline: 275 MW of long-lead AI generation capacity fully contracted and equipment-financed
current_signals.metric: 275 MW reciprocating-engine capacity secured; dedicated equipment financing closed; deliveries expected H2 2027 through H1 2028 for hyperscale AI/HPC infrastructure.
current_signals.read: New irreversible physical denominator. Customer/site allocation is not yet disclosed, so confidence is below the Monarch project, but equipment plus dedicated financing are real sunk commitments.

current_signals.headline: August revenue accelerated to a new monthly high
current_signals.metric: August revenue NT$514.81B, +10.1% MoM and +53.3% YoY; Jan-Aug revenue +39.3% YoY.
current_signals.read: Reinforces the active chip-revenue acceleration category; it does not add another sell point.

current_signals.headline: ERCOT begins formal verification RFIs for data-center interconnections
current_signals.metric: Data-center projects advancing through ERCOT must clear verification before moving forward; failure to satisfy the process excludes a large load from Batch Zero.
current_signals.read: Reinforces the same system-intervention category activated by PJM. It does not add a second sell point.

current_signals.headline: Australia ecosystem targets up to 2 GW of NVIDIA DSX AI-factory buildout by 2027
current_signals.metric: Partners are investing in DSX AI factories; CDC says >550 MW operating and 800 MW under construction; IREN cites its 800 MW Bundey campus. Overall NVIDIA headline is “up to 2 GW,” so not all capacity is counted as irreversible.
current_signals.read: Important pipeline confirmation, but the aggregate 2 GW is not added to the buy-clock denominator because the release mixes operating, under-construction and aspirational capacity.

current_signals.headline: Amazon-Qualcomm server-chip collaboration carries initial purchase commitments and up to $60B purchase-linked warrant vesting
current_signals.metric: Qualcomm warrant vests with commercial arrangements, binding purchase orders and actual purchases up to $60B; 3.75M warrant shares vested at issuance based on initial purchase commitments.
current_signals.read: Hard evidence of broadening hyperscaler silicon commitments beyond GPU incumbents. It confirms demand depth but remains the already-active chip category.

current_signals.headline: 2 GW equipment-delivery window begins
current_signals.metric: 2 GW natural-gas generator sets ordered; deliveries Sep-26 through Aug-27; 2 GW targeted online in 2027
current_signals.read: Strong buy-clock denominator: paid-for long-lead power equipment is physically entering the delivery phase.

current_signals.headline: AI system orders, backlog and recognized revenue accelerated again
current_signals.metric: $60.9B AI orders; $16.4B AI-server revenue; $95B AI backlog; first Vera Rubin rack systems shipping
current_signals.read: Hardware monetization is late-stage for the current tranche. The sell clock is 2/5 because power-delivery slippage has not reconverged.

current_signals.headline: Rubin is in full production and chip revenue is accelerating
current_signals.metric: $89.0B Data Center revenue (+117% YoY); Q3 revenue guide $108B; Rubin racks running at major cloud partners
current_signals.read: Current compute tranche is deep into silicon monetization. This advances the sell clock but is not bearish by itself.

current_signals.headline: Electrical orders and backlog remain elevated
current_signals.metric: Electrical Americas rolling orders +41%; Americas backlog +33% YoY; Electrical Global backlog +103%
current_signals.read: The downstream electrical layer is still being ordered aggressively, arguing that the next power denominator is still expanding.

current_signals.headline: Physical AI infrastructure is still converting to revenue
current_signals.metric: Q2 sales +24% YoY; FY26 organic sales growth guide 31% at midpoint
current_signals.read: Execution is tight but the MEP/cooling denominator is not rolling over.

current_signals.headline: Power and grid orders continue to accelerate
current_signals.metric: $24.2B Q2 orders (+88% organic); 116 GW gas equipment backlog + slot reservations; >$5B H1 data-center Electrification orders
current_signals.read: Broad physical-infrastructure commitment remains strong. Only project-specific AI MW are counted in denominator calculations.

weekly_history.note: Current tranche monetizing; next physical power/electrical tranche still expanding.
Irreversible power commitments expanded, but fresh PJM/ERCOT intervention activates the system-integration category while chip and server delivery acceleration remain active.

Amazon/Generac and Blockfusion/CoreWeave added hard 2027-28 physical/capacity commitments; CoreWeave put multi-rack Rubin into production and Crusoe closed $3.9B funding. No fourth independent sell category activated.

Power slippage and build-throughput gap activated: Project Jupiter force-majeure/pipeline delay plus a modeled 33 GW residual U.S. power shortfall; New Era, 2G Energy, Kodiak, Akamai and CleanSpark simultaneously hardened future physical demand.

Sell score remains maxed. New irreversible demand still expands: AIB/Nebius 50 MW with Oct. 1 utility service and 10/14-month hall targets, Enerflex adds a firm ~450 MW BTM generation-equipment award for 2027-28, and Amazon/Constellation supports a 190 MW nuclear uprate; Micron and Rubin rack deliveries keep hardware monetization fast.

derived.coverage_note: Withheld. Time-bounded usable-power additions can be identified (including Kodiak 76 MW gross BTM, AIB 50 MW critical IT, CleanSpark 175 MW critical IT, two 275 MW Energy Vault equipment tranches, and the Enerflex ~450 MW BTM generation award), but current hardware disclosures still lack sufficiently complete shipped quantities/configurations to convert the numerator into hardware-equivalent IT MW. Backlog dollars are not used as a substitute.

weekly_delta.headline: Amazon moves toward chip-backed SPV financing
weekly_delta.detail: FT reports roughly $8B of already-deployed NVIDIA Grace Blackwell chips may be financed through an SPV/leaseback structure. This reinforces delivery scale but is not a new order and adds no new sell point.

weekly_delta.headline: Enerflex adds ~450 MW of firm BTM generation deliveries
weekly_delta.detail: Contracted 450 MW natural-gas generation package for a North American data-center developer, with equipment deliveries starting in 2027 and completing in 2028.

weekly_delta.headline: JERA/Dell/RHAELM outline 400 MW Chiba pipeline — excluded from hard BUY clock
weekly_delta.detail: The >$15B project targets 2028 operations and BTM power, but the current document is an MoU with intended financing, so it remains pipeline-watch only.

weekly_delta.headline: Build-throughput gap remains independently active
weekly_delta.detail: AIB utility service starts Oct. 1, but 50 MW of contracted critical IT is targeted in two 25 MW halls around months 10 and 14.

weekly_delta.headline: Micron reinforces chip-revenue acceleration
weekly_delta.detail: FQ4 revenue reached $54.23B from $41.46B in FQ3; the chip-revenue category remains active without adding another point.

weekly_delta.headline: AIB/Nebius hardens 50 MW of critical IT
weekly_delta.detail: Binding 12-year customer deal is backed by a 65 MW utility ESA; project timeline explicitly targets 25 MW around month 10 and another 25 MW around month 14.

weekly_delta.headline: Amazon/Constellation locks long-duration nuclear supply
weekly_delta.detail: 20-year 690 MW agreement supports more than $3B of investment and roughly 190 MW of new nuclear output in 2030-2032.

weekly_delta.headline: FERC/PJM intervention remains live
weekly_delta.detail: PJM reliability backstop action and data-center cost allocation show system-level integration is still not keeping pace.

weekly_delta.headline: CleanSpark closes $2.276B Sandersville financing
weekly_delta.detail: Proceeds fund the build-out for a 175 MW critical-IT campus with deliveries expected to begin Q4 2027.

weekly_delta.headline: Power/COD slippage activates
weekly_delta.detail: Oracle issued a force-majeure notice on Project Jupiter while its gas pipeline slipped about six months. Oracle still says the 2028 campus schedule is intact.

weekly_delta.headline: Supermicro begins shipping Rubin NVL72 racks
weekly_delta.detail: Production shipments reinforce the active server/rack delivery category; reference blueprint quantities are not treated as shipped MW.

weekly_delta.headline: Energy Vault adds a second 275 MW generation tranche
weekly_delta.detail: 2G Energy order is scheduled for Q4 2027-Q3 2028 and is separate from the Sep. 10 Rolls-Royce MTU tranche.

weekly_delta.headline: Kodiak locks 76 MW of near-term BTM power
weekly_delta.detail: Six-year contract; deployment begins Q4 2026 and scales through Q1 2027.

power_slippage.reason: Project Jupiter carries an Oracle force-majeure notice and its supporting gas pipeline is about six months late, even though Oracle says the 2028 campus schedule remains intact.

build_throughput_gap.reason: AIB has utility service beginning Oct. 1 but targets only 25 MW critical IT around month 10 and the second 25 MW around month 14; this is direct evidence that powered capacity still takes many months to convert into usable AI halls. Morgan Stanley also modeled a 33 GW residual U.S. 2026-28 power shortfall after fast-power solutions.

chip_revenue_acceleration.reason: Micron FQ4 revenue accelerated to $54.23B from $41.46B sequentially; NVIDIA/TSMC acceleration remains live, and new AMD infrastructure orders add dated demand.

server_delivery_acceleration.reason: Supermicro is now shipping Vera Rubin NVL72 racks; CoreWeave/Dell/Oracle delivery acceleration remains active, and Akamai is front-loading component procurement for Anthropic.

system_intervention.reason: FERC approved/advanced PJM reliability backstop action tied to zones with data-center growth while ERCOT continues data-center impact RFIs and large-load screening.
